# I02 product-scope discovery — complete draft after plan comparison

**Date:** 2026-10-09 UTC  
**Plan reviewed:** exact `revealed-plan.md` generated by the required reveal command after `discovery.md` and `source-map.json` were saved.  
**Evidence:** source IDs/URLs/locators in `source-map.json`; substantive retained notes in `sources/`.  
**Execution boundary:** No product runtime, trial, setup, family-data entry, account configuration, reminder, outage simulation or screen-reader test has been performed. Validation items below are proposals, not completed tests.

## Executive recommendation

No specific product is proved viable yet. Run a short, synthetic-data procurement/trial screen before committing the six-month pilot. Lend Engine is the strongest low-cost lending-workflow lead, but its undated child-data policy, loan-field scope, backup discrepancy and cleaning gate require written answers and a working trial before any family record is entered. Check Blueprint OMS only if the clinic already has it. Compare AssetTiger or hosted Snipe-IT only for inventory/readiness or a split workflow if loan-level family data can remain in an independently approved, appropriately protected record; their reviewed evidence does not establish the needed per-loan data model. Cheqroom has explicit availability flags and maintenance work orders, but open work orders do not block availability, paid maintenance/operations add-ons are unpriced, and a two-site plan can use most of budget. AppSheet can support a custom Device/Loan model but documented last-writer-wins sync makes offline simultaneous checkout unsafe without stronger tested control; it also creates local-cache, support, and Twilio SMS considerations. myTurn merits a quote/demo, but evidence is too thin for ranking above those candidates.

For any selected approach, keep a persistent device record separate from a loan/family event, make return/cleaning/inspection a fail-closed availability gate, use minimal data, limit staff roles, protect the shared waiting-room workstation, offer plain-language preference-led reminders, and test the screen-reader user's complete workflow. Start online-first; when current availability cannot be confirmed, pause assignment or use a controlled, numbered paper queue with explicit reconciliation. Keep full clinical records and appointment integration out of this pilot. Resolve the director's fitting-note edit authority and identifiable-history retention decisions before configuration or purchase.

## Exact plan clause dispositions

Categories below use the required distinctions: **correction**, **optional enhancement**, **user decision**, **already covered**, **rejected**, or **uncertain**. A clause can be covered in principle while still needing a measurable definition or evidence. The plan is reviewed as written; nothing here silently changes its text.

### P1 — “Track each loan through preparation, assignment, return, cleaning, and availability for reassignment.”

**Disposition: correction + already-covered intent; add explicit safety-state and blocking semantics.** The clause covers the lifecycle concept, but “track” and “availability” do not state the necessary rule: returned devices must remain unavailable until cleaning and inspection pass, and only an authorized role can release the unit. Record the return event; then quarantine/clean/inspect. A failed inspection remains blocked and routes to repair/hold. The checkout/reservation control itself must consult the blocked status, not merely display a cleaning note or open maintenance task. Include device ID, site/location, timestamps and responsible role for operational transitions.

This correction is supported by the Cheqroom source distinction: configured availability flags may remove equipment from availability, whereas its operations overview explicitly says open work orders do not change availability. Snipe-IT's documentation offers pending/undeployable states as another potential gate, but does not prove the clinic's configured transition/permission behavior. Lend Engine's public page advertises cleaning/repair routing without proving a hard checkout lock. See retained product evidence in [`workflow-platforms.md`](sources/workflow-platforms.md), [`asset-trackers.md`](sources/asset-trackers.md), and [`lending-platforms.md`](sources/lending-platforms.md); source IDs SRC-02, SRC-09, SRC-11 and SRC-22.

**Optional enhancement:** expose separate states such as Ready, On loan, Returned—quarantined, Cleaning, Inspection pending, Inspection failed/repair, and Ready for reassignment; retain who/when/outcome and site. This is a useful way to make the safety rule legible, but state names and audit detail are implementation choices once the gate is enforced.

**Uncertain pending trial:** whether any listed vendor supports the exact blocking transition, exceptions, and authorized-release permissions in its purchased tier. Verify that open work order alone cannot bypass quarantine.

### P2 — “Associate loan records with the minimum patient and caregiver details needed for contact and handoff.”

**Disposition: correction + already-covered minimization intent; user decision for identity and fields.** “Minimum details” is directionally right but is too underspecified for build or vendor screening. A loan record needs the brief's concrete values: device ID, fitting settings specific to that loan, caregiver contact preference and return date, and when applicable an interpreter request. Keep those values on the loan/handoff record, not on the reusable device record or a globally visible member/device profile. Only a minimal patient/borrower reference should be used where operationally necessary; do not import a full clinical record or add diagnosis by default. Confirm field scope, visibility, export, deletion and history behavior with synthetic sequential loans before any family data is entered.

This is a model requirement inferred from the brief, not an already verified vendor capability. Reviewed Snipe-IT custom fields apply to the asset model. Reviewed Lend Engine, AssetTiger and Cheqroom pages do not prove the clinic's custom family data is transaction-scoped. Blueprint advertises loan history and agreements but public material does not settle its field model. See [`asset-trackers.md`](sources/asset-trackers.md), [`lending-platforms.md`](sources/lending-platforms.md), and [`workflow-platforms.md`](sources/workflow-platforms.md); SRC-02, SRC-04, SRC-05, SRC-08 and SRC-23.

**User decision:** director/clinical governance owner must specify who may create, view and amend fitting notes at handoff and after reassignment (connected to P5), who is the borrower identity of record, and how minimum details map to staff roles. The brief explicitly leaves authority for changing fitting notes unresolved. Do not invent this policy as a product default.

**Uncertain:** whether a product can retain a minimized historical loan while hiding prior family detail from the next borrower and shared workstation. Test both active and returned loans, search, exports, audit views, browser back/cache and deletion/retention.

### P3 — “Provide accessible status controls, including screen-reader labels and cues that do not depend on color.”

**Disposition: already covered in principle + correction to validation scope; optional enhancement for detailed criteria.** The clause correctly requires screen-reader labels and non-color status. Make acceptance explicit: a staff member using their actual screen reader and keyboard must complete the full core workflow, including lookup, creating/updating a loan, return, cleaning/inspection hold, pass/fail/release and reminder decision. Controls need announced names, roles, values and states; focus order and errors must be usable; status must be visible in text or another cue as well as color. W3C's use-of-color, keyboard and name/role/value guidance supports these checks (SRC-18–20; [`accessibility.md`](sources/accessibility.md)).

AssetTiger's Jan 2026 VPAT is vendor evidence based on WAVE and lists relevant supported/partial/untested rows, but it is not an end-to-end clinic task test and its front matter/table scope is not fully aligned. It cannot close this criterion (SRC-07; [`accessibility.md`](sources/accessibility.md)). Other product accessibility is unknown.

**Optional enhancement:** include the actual staff screen-reader user in acceptance trials and record blockers/remediation, rather than rely only on automated conformance reports. This converts the broad requirement into user-centered evidence; select a procurement standard only if the clinic wants one.

**Uncertain:** all candidate workflows until task-tested. No screen-reader or keyboard test was executed during research.

### P4 — “Support plain-language reminders and a staff view that limits exposure of other families' records.”

**Disposition: correction + already-covered objective; user decision for channel preferences.** Retain both goals, but define the minimum: reminders follow the caregiver's selected channel and consent, use clear plain language, avoid fitting settings/diagnosis or other unnecessary clinical detail, support opt-out and a clinic-approved interpreter path, and make failure/correction visible to staff. The waiting-room view must use individual staff accounts and least privilege and must not leave one family's information available to the next user through the prior screen, browser history/cache, exports or downloads; configure inactivity lock/re-auth and test the reset boundary.

The Lend Engine policy describes customizable day-before email content with item details, so privacy-minimized message content must be configured/verified; its undated child-data language remains a vendor suitability gate (SRC-03). AppSheet's SMS documentation requires custom Twilio setup and says the built-in channel was discontinued after 2025-04-21, so channel, price and recipient control cannot be assumed (SRC-17). AssetTiger describes roles/security but only as vendor claims (SRC-06). See [`lending-platforms.md`](sources/lending-platforms.md), [`low-code.md`](sources/low-code.md), and [`sources/index.md`](sources/index.md).

**User decision:** caregiver communication preference, consent/opt-out handling, who may view which fields, and whether reminder delivery is in the first pilot release need clinic approval. A reminder channel must not be inferred from a populated phone number.

**Uncertain:** actual session/cache behavior and message control in any candidate. Test synthetic family A then family B on the shared workstation, including lock, logout, reopen/back, export and print. Test reminder to a controlled number/address for correct preference and minimal content.

### P5 — “The role allowed to amend fitting notes after reassignment is a clinical governance decision.”

**Disposition: already covered + user decision.** The plan correctly treats authority as a clinic governance choice, not a vendor default or implementation detail for the researcher to decide. Preserve that open decision. The clinic's designated clinical/governance owner should decide whether the original author, current clinician, another named role or no one may amend after reassignment; define whether any correction is append-only with author/time/reason and what each role can see. The brief itself does not answer this.

**Optional enhancement:** record amendment actor/time/reason and preserve prior value in an approved audit trail if permitted; confirm whether corrections change only the active loan record or a clinical record system. This must not expand the pilot to full clinical-record migration.

**Uncertain:** exact policy, approver, workflow, and historical display; these require a clinic decision. No vendor feature claim resolves them.

### P6 — “Identifiable loan-history retention and any appointment-system connection remain open scope choices.”

**Disposition: already covered + user decision; add an explicit pilot boundary.** Keeping identifiable-history retention as an open choice is correct because the brief says the director has not decided. The clinic must set a retention period or trigger, deletion/anonymization rules, access, export and legal/records-owner approval before using identifiable history. Vendor defaults do not replace that decision. Lend Engine's privacy policy describes removal/anonymization and the pricing matrix shows a backup-tier distinction; obtain exact retention/backup/delete answers in writing (SRC-01, SRC-03). AppSheet mentions temporary caching and source-controlled data, not a complete clinic retention rule (SRC-16). See [`lending-platforms.md`](sources/lending-platforms.md) and [`low-code.md`](sources/low-code.md).

For this pilot, appointment-system connection should be **out of the approved first-year scope and budget**, not an implied deliverable. The brief allows it as a later possibility. Do not import the full clinical record to enable it. Revisit integration only after the pilot, a separate budget and privacy/design review. No vendor integration capability was investigated deeply because it is outside first-year scope.

**Optional enhancement:** document a pilot exit/export/deletion path and the post-pilot decision point. No particular retention duration, integration, or migration is recommended by this research.

**User decision:** director/records/privacy owner selects identifiable history retention and future integration timing/funding. If no retention decision is made, pause identifiable data entry rather than default to indefinite history.

**Uncertain:** applicable jurisdictional retention rules, agreement terms, vendor backup deletion timing and the clinic's existing record policy were not provided or reviewed; this is not a legal determination.

## Cross-clause findings and alternatives retained

### Data, roles and control model

A minimally sufficient design separates reusable **Device** state from per-family **Loan** events. Device fields: identifier, site/location and readiness/availability. Loan fields: device link, minimum borrower reference, fitting settings for this specific loan, caregiver preference, return date, optional interpreter request, actor/time and operational handoff events. The next family must not see previous loan details. A role model should distinguish loan creation/handoff, clinical-note amendment, cleaning/inspection, release, and system administration. These roles may overlap in a small team, but permissions and accountability still need to be explicit. Do not place fitting settings or family contact data on a reusable device asset unless the product can demonstrate they are isolated by loan and the clinic approves that design.

### Outage policy

AppSheet documents initial online launch/cache conditions and last-writer-wins for concurrent edits to one row (SRC-14, SRC-15); AssetTiger says its mobile scanning queues locally but documents no collision policy in the reviewed FAQ (SRC-06). No source establishes safe two-site authoritative offline checkout. Therefore do not promise simultaneous offline allocation. Candidate pilot control: online-first, fail closed if authoritative current availability cannot be read; if a director approves continuity, use a controlled numbered paper queue with a single custodian and reconciliation log, then reconcile on restored connection before any device is marked ready. Test this process across both locations. This is a proposed operational control, not a capability any product demonstrated.

### Commercial and support fit

Public annual/list pricing suggests some choices fit budget comfortably (AssetTiger $220; hosted Snipe-IT $399.99; Lend Engine Plus $300 or Business $600), but terms, costs, current tiers and required support remain unverified. Cheqroom Business starts at $3,300 per admin annually for up to three sites, with added maintenance/operations fees and minimum admin counts; two admins at starting price would be $6,600 before add-ons. AppSheet Core ten paid seats list at $1,200 annually, before licensing/data/SMS dependencies. Blueprint price was not found; conditional on existing access. These values are vendor pages as accessed Oct 9, 2026, not quotes or total cost.

No sysadmin argues against self-hosting and unmaintained custom code. Hosted service still needs defined support, export/deletion, backup/restore, role management and a named clinic owner. The Snipe-IT issue/fix/release chain shows why the current version and permissions need task verification: a v8.4.1 issue led to a distinct maintenance permission in v8.5.0, while cross-company history remained a separate concern; v8.8.0 was listed as current at retrieval (SRC-24–27; [`release-chain.md`](sources/release-chain.md)). This is relevant evolution evidence, not proof of general product failure.

### Candidate ranking is conditional, not a selection

1. **Lend Engine:** best price/workflow lead; child-data/privacy policy and transaction model block identifiable use until written resolution; prove hard cleaning gate, backups and accessibility.
2. **Blueprint OMS:** targeted conditional inquiry only if already licensed; domain fit strong, public pricing and suitability evidence absent.
3. **AssetTiger:** low-cost inventory trial; verify transaction-scoped family data, quarantine, sync collision, privacy and task accessibility. Could serve a device-only register, but split systems add reconciliation risk.
4. **Hosted Snipe-IT:** low-cost supported hosting and flexible operational state; reviewed custom fields are asset-scoped. Consider device/readiness only unless loan-level privacy model is proved. Pin supported version and test the permission chain.
5. **Cheqroom:** strongest explicit maintenance/availability workflow evidence, with open-work-order caveat. Quote add-ons/admin seats and trial permissions/data/accessibility; likely budget pressure.
6. **AppSheet:** custom data model and low list price; do not rely on simultaneous offline conflict-prone checkout; requires app ownership, data/security/retention design and Twilio if SMS.
7. **myTurn:** request quote and demonstration if needed for lending-library alternative; evidence insufficient to establish core constraints.
8. **Numbered paper outage queue:** process fallback only; requires secure minimal records, clear custody and reconciliation owner; not a stand-alone software solution.

A reasonable purchase gate is: written child/family-data answer and contract terms; verified loan-level data isolation; an enforced return/cleaning/inspection release gate; actual screen-reader task completion; safe shared-workstation boundary; two-site/outage control; acceptable quote and support/exit terms; and director decisions on note amendments and retention. A candidate that fails any of the data-isolation, readiness, privacy, accessibility or cost gates should not enter the pilot as the authoritative workflow.

## Proposed validation versus executed work

| Proposed check | What it distinguishes | Execution status |
|---|---|---|
| Synthetic sequential loan on one reusable device | Loan-event fields stay with the right family; next borrower cannot view prior fitting/contact/interpreter data; export/delete follows policy. | Not run |
| Returned device checkout attempt | Return starts quarantine; reservation/check-out is blocked during cleaning and failed inspection; only authorized passing inspection releases availability. Include open-ticket-only attempt. | Not run |
| Roles and shared workstation | Reception/clinician/cleaner/release roles can perform only allowed actions; after family A, lock/log out/reopen and verify family B sees no A data, including back/cache/download/export. | Not run |
| Two-site outage/concurrency | No duplicate loan or unsafe release during stale/offline state; paper fallback is reconciled without losing custody or audit. | Not run |
| Screen-reader/keyboard end-to-end | Staff member completes lookup, handoff, return, inspection and reminder with announced controls, focus/errors, and status cues independent of color. | Not run |
| Reminder preference test | Correct channel/recipient; caregiver preference, plain language, minimal data, consent/opt-out and failed-delivery handling work. | Not run |
| Procurement review | Written cost including minimum seats/add-ons, privacy/security/retention/backups, support, exit/export and age/child-data treatment meet clinic approval. | Not run |
| Snipe-IT release/permission case if considered | Current supported hosted build; restricted user maintenance entry/attachments and site/company history scope function as required. | Not run |

### Work actually performed

The researcher read the assignment, exact input-map, exact I02 brief and exact revealed plan; reviewed public primary-source pages and release records listed in the source map; wrote retained source notes, source map and brief-based discovery before plan reveal; and validated the source-map JSON syntax. No live product, trial, app, configuration, contract, data transfer, reminder, concurrency/outage or screen-reader check was executed. No legal, jurisdictional or security audit was performed. All such checks are proposals.
